Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.

Issues.Title: Strong name signature not valid
Issues.Body:
Since I've ported a ClickOnce application from .NET Framework 4.6.1 to .NET Standard 2.0, the message _"Strong assembly name signature not valid for **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**"_ appears when trying to install or update the application. So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

```sh
> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly
```

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:

    - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment
      - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Authoring
        - **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths" (#43153)

Issues.Title: Support roslyn-language-server tool installation on FreeBSD
Issues.Body:
### Problem

The new `roslyn-language-server` .NET tool cannot currently be installed with the stable FreeBSD SDK. On FreeBSD 15.1 amd64 with the native FreeBSD Ports SDK 9.0.115/runtime 9.0.14 (`RID: freebsd.15-x64`):

```text
$ dotnet tool install roslyn-language-server --prerelease --tool-path ./roslyn-tool
The settings file in the tool's NuGet package is invalid: Format version is higher than supported.
This tool may not be supported in this SDK version. Update your SDK.
```

Roslyn main now requires .NET 10 and `LanguageServerPublish.props` publishes apphosts only for Windows, Linux, Linux-musl and macOS RIDs. FreeBSD Ports currently packages stable .NET 9/8; `lang/dotnet-devel` is an unpackaged .NET 10 alpha bootstrap port.

### Existing native evidence

This is not a request based only on package metadata. Using native FreeBSD .NET 9 and the platform-neutral managed Roslyn 4.14.0 language-server payload, we validated on FreeBSD 15.1 amd64:

- C# console build and execution
- LSP initialize
- completion and diagnostics in Code - OSS
- hover and go-to-definition
- rename returning the expected edits

The downstream integration and exact limitations are recorded in [EriduOs PR #12](https://github.com/tomblanchard312/EriduOs/pull/12).

### Suggested direction

Once a supported FreeBSD .NET 10 SDK/runtime is available, could the tool packaging either:

1. publish `freebsd-x64`/`freebsd-arm64` framework-dependent assets, or
2. include a portable managed fallback that launches `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.LanguageServer.dll` through the current `dotnet` host when no platform apphost is packaged?

I can prepare and test the Roslyn-side change against native FreeBSD once the .NET 10 prerequisite is available. I did not add FreeBSD RIDs blindly because the current official build cannot restore/test the corresponding .NET 10 host packs, and doing so would create an unverified package.

Issues.Title: Don't report CA1704 for parameters named _
Issues.Body:
Related to dotnet/roslyn-analyzers#5183, follow-up to #85161

@jasonmalinowski @CyrusNajmabadi you mentioned being open to a few more special cases if they present themselves; this is the next one.

### Problem

`CA1704` reports `_` as an unmeaningful parameter name:

```csharp
[ClassInitialize]
public static void ClassInitialize(TestContext _) { }
//                                             ^ CA1704
```

`_` is the established way to mark a parameter that a signature requires but the method does not use. IDE0060 (remove unused parameter) explicitly skips parameters named `_`, `_1`, … for that reason (`IsSymbolWithSpecialDiscardName`). So the two analyzers contradict each other:

- keep `_` → CA1704
- rename to e.g. `context` → IDE0060

On one mid-size codebase, after #85161, 20 of the remaining 103 CA1704 findings were parameters named `_`.

## Change

A parameter named `_` is no longer reported by CA1704.

- `_1`, `__` etc. were never reported (longer than one character, no words to spell check)
- fields named `_` are unaffected (the `_` prefix is stripped, nothing remains)
- every other single-letter parameter is still reported

## Notes for review

- Only removes diagnostics, so it cannot break existing builds.
- No new rule, option or descriptor change, so no AnalyzerReleases entry is needed.
- No new public API.

## Tests

In `IdentifiersShouldBeSpelledCorrectlyTests`:

- `_` as method, constructor and delegate parameter → no diagnostic

Issues.Title: Avoid compilation stalls when source files are deleted
Issues.Body:
Resolves #86236

Deletion notifications can invalidate document text before a project reload removes the documents. Applying those pending text updates can load missing files and stall compilation while the text loader retries.

`UpdateOrRemoveDocumentsAction` merges consecutive pending source-document updates and removals. It retains the original project state, the final project state, and the affected document IDs. Surviving documents use their final syntax trees. Removed documents have their original trees removed without loading replacement text. Other translation kinds prevent merging, and the text loader's retry behavior remains unchanged.

Earlier in-process language-server project-loading verification reduced the semantic-model wait after deleting 20 files from about 20.5 seconds to about 0.6 ms for individual deletions and 14.9 ms for directory deletion. These were individual measurements, not benchmark averages. Those server-specific tests are not retained in the final PR.

Issues.Title: Find and remove unnecessary Razor using directives for dotnet format
Issues.Body:
## Summary

This PR adds `RazorUnnecessaryDirectives` to `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Razor.DotNetFormat`. The new API finds the `@using` directives that a `.razor` component does not need, and it removes them.

`dotnet format` consumes this package, as added in dotnet/sdk#56563. With this API, `dotnet format style` can report these directives as IDE0005 and remove them from the command line. A CI pipeline can then catch them, as the editor already does with RZ0005.

## Motivation

Visual Studio fades an unnecessary `@using` directive in a `.razor` file, and it offers a code action to remove the directive (dotnet/razor#8548, dotnet/razor#4521). No command-line tool reports the same problem:

- `IDE0005_gen` is not configurable, and it does not run on build.
- Raw CS8019 results are wrong for Razor. Generated code refers to components by their fully qualified names, so a `@using` that is needed only to find a component looks unused to the compiler.
- The filter that corrects this, `RazorCodeDocument.IsDirectiveUsed`, needs tag helper data. Only the Razor source generator has that data, so an analyzer cannot do this check.

`Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Razor.DotNetFormat` already reads the generator host output for dotnet format. This API uses that output to give dotnet format the same result as the editor.

## Changes

### New public API

```csharp
public static class RazorUnnecessaryDirectives
{
    public static Task<ImmutableArray<TextSpan>> GetUnnecessaryUsingDirectiveSpansAsync(Project project, DocumentId documentId, CancellationToken cancellationToken);
    public static Task<SourceText?> RemoveUnnecessaryUsingDirectivesAsync(Project project, DocumentId documentId, CancellationToken cancellationToken);
}
```

The API reports a `@using` directive in a component as unnecessary in either of these cases:

1. The compiler reports its using as unused (CS8019) in both generated documents, and `IsDirectiveUsed` shows that Razor did not need it to find a component. These are the same rules as RZ0005 in `RazorTranslateDiagnosticsService` and `RemoteDiagnosticsService`.
2. The directive repeats a directive of an `_Imports.razor` file that applies to the component. The lowering phase emits only one copy of a repeated using, so the compiler cannot report the repeat. This rule is new, and the editor does not report it. Removing the directive is always safe, because the imports file keeps the namespace in scope.

The API returns nothing for the following documents:

- imports files, because a directive in an imports file applies to many components
- legacy `.cshtml` files
- projects without the Razor source generator

`RemoveUnnecessaryUsingDirectivesAsync` removes a directive together with its line break when the directive is the only content on its line.

### Shared removal rule

The line removal rule of `UsingDirectiveHelper.GetRemoveDirectiveEdit` moves to the new `SourceText.GetDirectiveRemovalSpan` in `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Razor.Workspaces.Shared`. The editor code action and dotnet format now remove directives in the same way. The editor behavior does not change.

### Lookup without exceptions

`RazorProjectGeneratorRunResult` gets `TryGetSourceGeneratedDocumentAsync`, because a fallback component has no declaration document.

## Points for review

**1. The compiler drops the unused usings of the declaration tree.** On a compilation that has not bound anything, `SemanticModel.GetDiagnostics()` returns the expected CS8019 results when it is called for the declaration tree first. If the implementation tree of the same component is bound first, the declaration tree then returns no CS8019 results. The API therefore reads the declaration tree first, on `compilation.Clone()`. Another caller can already have bound the project's cached compilation. This might be a compiler bug. I can open a separate issue if the team agrees.

**2. Documentation mode.** CS8019 is reported only when `DocumentationMode` is not `None` (`Compilation.ReportUnusedImportsInTree`). Most projects do not set `GenerateDocumentationFile`, so the API replaces the generated trees with copies that have the same root and `DocumentationMode.Parse`.

**3. The repeat rule goes beyond RZ0005.** Is it acceptable to report a repeat of an `_Imports.razor` directive in the API? The editor could use the same rule later.

**4. Known gap.** The API keeps a directive for a parent namespace of the component, for example `@using MyApp.Pages` in a component in `MyApp.Pages.Admin`. `IsDirectiveUsed` credits that directive for component discovery, and the editor also keeps it.

## Testing

- **New tests:** `RazorUnnecessaryDirectivesTest` adds 15 tests that cover these cases:
  - unused namespaces, and namespaces that code or markup uses
  - namespaces that a component needs, and namespaces of components that the file does not use
  - repeats of `_Imports.razor` directives, including repeats that code or a component needs
  - imports files and legacy files
  - projects without documentation comments, and projects without the generator
  - removal with LF and CRLF line endings
- **Existing tests:** all 48 tests in `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Razor.DotNetFormat.UnitTests` pass. The 43 tests for `RemoveUnnecessaryDirectiveTests` and `SortAndConsolidateUsingsTests` in `Microsoft.VisualStudioCode.RazorExtension.UnitTests` pass.
- **Analyzers:** the changed projects build with `-p:RunAnalyzersDuringBuild=true` and show no warnings.
- **End-to-end:** I ran a local dotnet format build with this API in `style` mode.
  - On a `dotnet new blazor` project, it reported the unnecessary directives, removed them, and passed a second check. The project still builds.
  - On a production Blazor application, it reported 20 directives. Trial builds confirmed each of the 20 as unnecessary. It reported no false positives.

 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/86283)

Issues.Title: NullableWalker returns pooled `Variables` collections twice when lambda analysis throws, corrupting nullable analysis process-wide
Issues.Body:
**Version used:** Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 5.9.0 (also checked by reading `NullableWalker.cs` on `main` at 7ed110c0f9, 2026-10-16: the code is unchanged)
**Runtime:** .NET 10.0.12, macOS 27.2 arm64 (repro). Originally seen on .NET 10.0.14, Linux x64 (GitHub Actions ubuntu-26.04).

## Summary

When an exception escapes the analysis of a lambda or local function body in `NullableWalker.AnalyzeLocalFunctionOrLambda`, `_variables` is not restored to its container, because the restore (`_variables = _variables.Container!;`) is after the `try`/`finally` and not in the `finally`. `NullableWalker.Free()` then frees the nested `Variables` twice:

1. once in the loop over `_nestedFunctionVariables.Values`, as `GetOrCreateNestedFunctionVariables` registered it there, and
2. once in the loop over the `_variables` / `Container` chain, which still starts at the nested `Variables`.

`Variables.Free()` returns `_variableSlot` (`PooledDictionary<VariableIdentifier, int>`), `_variableTypes` (`PooledDictionary<Symbol, TypeWithAnnotations>`) and `_variableBySlot` (`ArrayBuilder<VariableIdentifier>`) to their static `ObjectPool`s. Each one is put in its pool twice, so the next two `Variables` instances created anywhere in the process share the same collections. Nullable analysis in **any later, unrelated compilation** then fails at random with `NullReferenceException` in `GetDefaultState`, `IndexOutOfRangeException` in `Variables.Populate` or `InheritNullableStateOfTrackableStruct`, `ArgumentException` "An item with the same key has already been added" in `Variables.Populate` / `GetOrCreateSlot`, `ArgumentException` / `ArgumentNullException` in `Variables.CreateSnapshot`, or "Collection was modified" when two threads compile methods in parallel.

The exception that starts it does not need to be visible. `CancelledByStackGuardException` is caught by `NullableWalker.Analyze(NullableWalker walker, ...)` and reported as **CS8078** ("An expression is too long or complex to compile"), so a single file with deeply nested code in a lambda silently poisons the process. Any other exception thrown while a lambda body is analyzed has the same effect, and the crashes it causes inside lambdas free the shared collections again, so a poisoned process keeps getting worse.

```csharp
private void AnalyzeLocalFunctionOrLambda(...)
{
    ...
    _variables = GetOrCreateNestedFunctionVariables(_variables, lambdaOrFunctionSymbol);
    this.State = state.CreateNestedMethodState(_variables);
    var previousSlot = _snapshotBuilderOpt?.EnterNewWalker(lambdaOrFunctionSymbol) ?? -1;
    try
    {
        ...
        VisitAlways(lambdaOrFunction.Body);   // CancelledByStackGuardException, or any other exception
        ...
    }
    finally
    {
        _snapshotBuilderOpt?.ExitWalker(this.SaveSharedState(), previousSlot);
    }

    _variables = _variables.Container!;      // skipped when the body throws
    this.State = oldState;
    ...
}
```

This is not new in #82784 ("Validate pooled objects in compiler tests"), which changed `Free()` to walk the `Container` chain: before it, `Free()` called `_variables.Free()`, which freed the same nested `Variables` a second time.

## Steps to reproduce

`Repro.csproj`:

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp" Version="5.9.0" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

`Program.cs`:

```csharp
using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis;
using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp;

var references = ((string)AppContext.GetData("TRUSTED_PLATFORM_ASSEMBLIES")!).Split(Path.PathSeparator)
    .Where(path => Path.GetFileName(path) is "System.Runtime.dll" or "System.Private.CoreLib.dll")
    .Select(path => MetadataReference.CreateFromFile(path))
    .ToArray();

CSharpCompilation Compile(string source) => CSharpCompilation.Create(
    "Test",
    [CSharpSyntaxTree.ParseText(source)],
    references,
    new CSharpCompilationOptions(OutputKind.DynamicallyLinkedLibrary, nullableContextOptions: NullableContextOptions.Enable));

// An unrelated, valid program that uses a lambda. It compiles fine in a fresh process.
const string Victim = """
    class D
    {
        void N(string s) { System.Func<int> f = () => s.Length; }
    }
    """;

Console.WriteLine($"Before: {Compile(Victim).GetDiagnostics().Length} diagnostics");

// A lambda whose body is nested deeply enough for NullableWalker's stack guard to fire, but not the binder's.
// The depth at which this happens depends on the stack size of the machine, so increase it until CS8078 is reported.
for (var depth = 500; depth <= 3000; depth += 25)
{
    var tuple = string.Concat(Enumerable.Repeat("(0, ", depth)) + "0" + new string(')', depth);
    var deep = $$"""
        class C
        {
            void N() { System.Func<object> f = () => {{tuple}}; }
        }
        """;

    // Thread pool thread, as in an IDE or in parallel compilation
    var errors = Task.Run(() => Compile(deep).GetDiagnostics()).Result.Where(d => d.Severity == DiagnosticSeverity.Error).ToArray();
    if (errors.Length == 0)
        continue;

    Console.WriteLine($"Depth {depth}: {string.Join(", ", errors.Select(e => e.Id).Distinct())}");
    try
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"After: {Compile(Victim).GetDiagnostics().Length} diagnostics");
    }
    catch (Exception ex)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"After: {ex}");
        return 1;
    }
}

Console.WriteLine("Not reproduced");
return 0;
```

`dotnet run -c Release`

The depth at which the nullable walker's stack guard fires, but not the binder's, depends on the stack size, so the program increases the depth until it gets there (975 on macOS arm64). For a deterministic repro in the Roslyn test suite, set `compilation.TestOnlyCompilationData = new NullableWalker.NullableAnalysisData(maxRecursionDepth: 30)` on a compilation with `System.Func<object> f = () => M(M(M(...)));` (50 nested calls). Pooled-object validation from #82784 should then report the double free directly.

## Expected behavior

The deep lambda reports CS8078, and the next, unrelated compilation (`class D { void N(string s) { System.Func<int> f = () => s.Length; } }`) compiles with no diagnostics.

## Actual behavior

The deep lambda reports CS8078, then `GetDiagnostics()` on the unrelated compilation throws:


## Impact

Hosts that keep one process for many compilations are affected: the IDE / OOP server, the compiler server (VBCSCompiler), and analyzer test or fuzzing harnesses. After one file hits CS8078 inside a lambda (or any exception during lambda nullable analysis), unrelated files fail with crashes that cannot be reproduced in a fresh process.

## Found by

Fuzzing Meziantou.Analyzer (run https://github.com/meziantou/Meziantou.Analyzer/actions/runs/41287436478): 72 findings across about 40 analyzers, code fixers and plain `Compilation.GetDiagnostics` calls, none of which reproduce on their own. A probe that checks the Roslyn pools for duplicate entries after each input confirms that the deep-lambda input above leaves the same `PooledDictionary` in the pool twice.

Issues.Title: Restore the nullable walker state when the analysis of a lambda throws
Issues.Body:
Fixes #86276

`AnalyzeLocalFunctionOrLambda` restored `_variables` (and the other fields it saves) after its `try`/`finally` instead of in the `finally`. When the analysis of the body throws, `_variables` still references the variables of the nested function. For instance, the stack guard throws on deeply nested code, and `NullableWalker.Analyze` catches the exception and reports CS8078. `Free()` then frees those variables twice: once from `_nestedFunctionVariables`, and once from the `_variables` chain.

`Variables.Free()` returns pooled dictionaries and builders to static pools, so they end up twice in their pools. From then on, two `Variables` instances of any later compilation in the process can share the same collections. The nullable analysis of unrelated code then fails with a `NullReferenceException` in `GetDefaultState`, an `ArgumentException` or `IndexOutOfRangeException` in `Variables.Populate`, or `Collection was modified` when methods are compiled in parallel. The crashes don't reproduce in a fresh process.

The fix moves the restore into the `finally` block, after `ExitWalker`, which still needs the variables of the nested function to create its snapshot.

The test analyzes a lambda whose body hits the stack guard, then compiles unrelated code that uses lambdas. Like the other stack guard tests, it only runs in Release: in Debug, the stack guard path fails the nullable analysis verification and the pooled object validation.

Issues.Title: EE: Locals should list an in-scope local that has the same name as a parameter (F#)
Issues.Body:
> **TL;DR:** When an F# local reuses a parameter's name, Visual Studio's Locals window shows the parameter instead of the local. My proposed fix in the C# expression evaluator passes an IL-based regression test, and with it Visual Studio 2026 lists the local. The change adds 22 lines to `CompilationContext.cs` and one test. May I open a PR with this approach?

This is dotnet/fsharp#12409. The cause is in the C# expression evaluator, which Visual Studio also uses for F# frames.

**Version Used**: Visual Studio Community 2026 18.11.3 on Windows Server 2025 x64. Its C# expression evaluator is 5.11.0-1.26424.5 (`fcacacf8`). Visual Studio Community 2026 18.7.3 on Windows 11 ARM64 (evaluator 5.7.0-1.26254.3, `c86410db`) shows the same bug. The code links below are at `main` `c0c4182`.

**Steps to Reproduce**:

1. Build this F# program with .NET SDK 10.0.402, Debug, portable PDB:

   ```fsharp
   let inp = seq { 1 .. 3 }
   let h3 x =
       for x in inp do
          printfn $"hello, x = {x}"
          printfn "hello"

   h3 10
   ```

2. Set a breakpoint on the `printfn $"hello, x = {x}"` line and debug.
3. When it stops, look at the Locals window and evaluate `x`.

The PDB has a `LocalVariable` named `x` in a scope that covers the loop body.

**Expected Behavior**: Locals shows the loop's `x` (1 on the first stop), the value that evaluating `x` returns.

**Actual Behavior**: Locals shows the parameter `x = 10` and the `Type variables` node, and no loop `x`. Evaluating `x` returns 1, then 2. On both machines, I recorded this through EnvDTE (`Debugger.CurrentStackFrame.Locals` and `Debugger.GetExpression("x")`) at two stops of the loop.

**Cause**: In `CompilationContext.CompileGetLocals`, [lines 402-411](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/c0c418248c9760d912747320a10392d0aab49cd2/src/ExpressionEvaluator/CSharp/Source/ExpressionCompiler/CompilationContext.cs#L402-L411) add the name of each parameter, other than generated and display class parameters, to `itemsAdded`. [Lines 480-484](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/c0c418248c9760d912747320a10392d0aab49cd2/src/ExpressionEvaluator/CSharp/Source/ExpressionCompiler/CompilationContext.cs#L480-L484) then skip every in-scope local whose name is in that set. C# rejects this shadowing with CS0136.

**Proposed change**: When an ordinary in-scope local has a parameter's name, list the local in the parameter's place. [Lines 413-433](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/c0c418248c9760d912747320a10392d0aab49cd2/src/ExpressionEvaluator/CSharp/Source/ExpressionCompiler/CompilationContext.cs#L413-L433) already do this for a captured parameter's display class field. The arguments-only query (`argumentsOnly: true`) still lists the parameter.

I checked the change in Visual Studio 18.11.3 on x64. I built Roslyn at `fcacacf8`, the commit that version ships, with the change applied, and deployed it to the `RoslynDev` experimental hive with Roslyn's `-deployExtensions` build. With the same program and breakpoint, Locals listed the loop's `x` (1, then 2), and `StackFrame.Arguments` still listed the parameter `x = 10`. The same build without the change, in the same hive, again showed the parameter `x = 10` in Locals and no loop `x`.

The new test in `LocalsTests.cs` builds the method from IL, because C# cannot declare a local with the same name as a parameter. On the ARM64 machine, the test failed without the change and passed with it. It also fails if I remove either the check for an arguments-only query or the check for a matching name. The whole C# `ExpressionCompiler` test project, run on .NET Framework, reported 816 tests: 752 passed, 64 skipped, 0 failed.

> [!NOTE]
> I prepared this issue with AI assistance (Anthropic Claude, reviewed by OpenAI Codex) and reviewed it before filing.

Issues.Title: Warn usages from `is TypeParam?` in context of nullable warnings enabled
Issues.Body:
<!-- This issue template is **only** for analyzers related to code style. -->
<!-- To propose a semantic/code quality analyzer, please follow the guidelines at https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn-analyzers/blob/main/GuidelinesForNewRules.md. -->

**Brief description:**

Consider an expression `v is TypeParameter?` in context of `#nullable enable` which `TypeParameter` is not restricted to non-nullable struct. While developers may intuitively expect the result is `true` when `v` is `null`, as they may misunderstood the `TypeParameter?` as an NRT. I suggest to add 2 new warning level diagnostic for such counterintuitive cases.

**Languages applicable:**

C#

**Code example that the analyzer should report:**

```C#
// From here on, the nullable warning has been enabled. Nullable annotation flag is not considered.
// Note: the nullable warning can be typically enabled by explicit `#nullable enable` or setting the `<Nullable>` MSBuild property 
class G1NW<T1> where T1 : struct
{
    void M1(object? v) => v is T1?; // should report the <DIAGID1>
    void M2(object? v) => v is Nullable<T1>; // should report the <DIAGID1>
}

class G2NW<T2>
{
    void M1(object? v) => v is T2?; // should report the <DIAGID2>
    void M2(object? v) => v is Nullable<T2>; // should report the <DIAGID2>
}

class G3NW<TClass> where TClass : class
{
    void M1(object? v) => v is TClass?; // already governed by CS8650
}

class CNW
{
    void M1<T1>(object? v) where T1 : struct
         => v is T1?; // should report the <DIAGID1>
    void M2<T1>(object? v) where T1 : struct
         => v is Nullable<T1>; // should report the <DIAGID1>

    void M3<T2>(object? v) => v is T2?; // should report the <DIAGID2>
    void M4<T2>(object? v) => v is Nullable<T2>; // should report the <DIAGID2>

    void M5<TClass>(object? v)  where TClass : class
        => v is TClass?; // already governed by CS8650
}
```

**Code example that the analyzer should NOT report:**
```C#
// From here on, the nullable warning are NOT enabled in contrast. Nullable annotation flag is not considered.
// Note: the nullable warning can be typically disabled by explicit `#nullable disable` or omitting the `<Nullable>` MSBuild property 
class G1ND<T1> where T1 : struct
{
    void M1(object? v) => v is T1?; // should not report since the nullable warnings are not enabled
    void M2(object? v) => v is Nullable<T1>; // should not report, same as G1ND.M1()
}

class G2ND<T2>
{
    void M1(object? v) => v is T2?; // should not report, same as G1ND.M1()
    void M2(object? v) => v is Nullable<T2>; // should not report, same as G1ND.M1()
}

class G3ND<TClass> where TClass : class
{
    void M1(object v) => v is TClass?; // already governed by CS8650
}

class CND
{
    void M1<T1>(object v) where T1 : struct
         => v is T1?; // should not report,  same as G1ND.M1()
    void M2<T1>(object v) where T1 : struct
         => v is Nullable<T1>; // should not report,  same as G1ND.M1()

    void M3<T2>(object v) => v is T2?; // should not report,  same as G1ND.M1()
    void M4<T2>(object v) => v is Nullable<T2>; // should not report,  same as G1ND.M1()

    void M5<TClass>(object v)  where TClass : class
        => v is TClass?; // already governed by CS8650
}
```

**Additional information:**

Original discussion about `is TypeParam?`:
https://github.com/dotnet/csharplang/discussions/10404#discussion-11141052

Suggestion of opening a analyzer request issue in this repo I received:
https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/discussions/86269#discussioncomment-19301611


**Documentation requirements:**

When this analyzer is implemented, it must be documented by following the steps at [Documentation for IDE CodeStyle analyzers](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/contributing/Documentation%20for%20IDE%20CodeStyle%20analyzers.md).

1. [ ] Allocate diagnostic IDs
2. [ ] Compose formal diagnostic text resources
      - [ ] `<DIAGID1>` Note: contributed by nullable value type occurred in RHS of `is`-type.
      - [ ] `<DIAGID2>` Note: contributed by non-reference-non-value-type-constrained type parameter with nullable annotation, or nullable value type.
3. [ ] Update the `dotnet/docs`
4. [ ] Write diagnostic documentation pages
      - [ ] `<DIAGID1>`
      - [ ] `<DIAGID2>` 
6. [ ] Update tabular diagnostic indices

Issues.Title: dotnetup: support daily builds in admin mode (including RTM and servicing build identity)
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`dotnetup` admin mode (Windows installer bundles) cannot install daily builds today. It is expected to gain daily build support, and when it does, RTM and servicing daily builds need the same build-identity handling that archive installs received in #56913.

## Current behavior

- Admin mode installs through `WindowsBundleArtifact`, which forces `RequireReleasesJsonSignature = true` ([WindowsBundleArtifact.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/release/dnup/src/Installer/dotnetup.Library/WindowsInstaller/WindowsBundleArtifact.cs)).
- Daily channels resolve only from the public blob feed, and that path calls `ThrowIfReleasesJsonSignatureRequired`, which fails with `AdminModeSignatureRequired` ([DotnetDownloader.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/release/dnup/src/Installer/Microsoft.Dotnet.Installation/Internal/DotnetDownloader.cs)).
- `ResolveManifestEntry_RequestExpectsReleasesJsonSignature_RejectsUnsignedSource` in `DotnetDownloaderBlobFeedTests` asserts this for bundle requests.

So `dotnetup sdk install 11-daily` in admin mode fails before any download.

## Work needed

1. Decide how admin mode trusts daily bundles. They are not covered by the signed releases.json; Authenticode verification of the `.exe` may be enough (related: #54278).
2. Allow bundle requests through the blob feed path when that trust model is satisfied.

## Context: RTM and servicing daily builds (from #56913)

RTM and servicing daily builds live in a build-identity directory (for example `Sdk/11.0.100-rtm.26552.115/`) but publish files named with the release version (`dotnet-sdk-11.0.100-win-x64.exe`) and install into the release-version folder (`sdk/11.0.100`). #56913 handles this for archives. For bundles:

**Already handled**
- The blob feed fallback to the untagged file name also covers `.exe`, and `WindowsBundleArtifact.ProductVersion` passes the on-disk version through, so post-install validation and `--update-global-json` should use `11.0.100`.

**Gaps to address**
- **False "already installed".** Bundle installs decide "already installed" by validating the `sdk/11.0.100` folder. A different build in that folder (the stable release, or another RTM daily) is reported as already installed. Archive installs avoid this by comparing the commit on line 1 of each `.version` file in the archive with the folder on disk ([#56913, aa10c7e](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/56913/commits/aa10c7e4e2d56c90dc140e0bfb1dce9a457d93c3)). Bundles do not expose those files without extracting.
- **Windows Installer behavior is unverified.** Two different builds with the same product version (for example `11.0.100` RTM daily vs `11.0.100` release) may be treated as the same product by Windows Installer, resulting in a no-op or repair instead of the requested build. This needs to be tested.

**Possible approach**
- Compare the existing folder's `.version` commit (first line) with the requested build's commit. The commit for a daily build could come from the blob feed (for example `productCommit-<rid>.txt`), so the check would not depend on extracting the bundle.
- Verified facts on `.version`: SDK files contain commit / version / RID / full build version / feature band; runtime, ASP.NET Core and Windows Desktop files contain commit / version. A stable release is a promoted daily build, so its commit equals that daily's commit, and runtimes bundled in later SDK feature bands keep the 1xx build's commit.

## Related

- #56913: RTM and servicing daily build support for archive installs
- #56921: automatically replacing installs that share an on-disk version
- #56670: original daily install failure

Issues.Title: dotnetup: UX enhancement - automatically replace installs that share an on-disk version, with in-use detection
Issues.Body:
Follow-up from https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/56913#discussion_r4461189250.

## Problem

RTM and servicing daily builds have a build identity such as `11.0.100-rtm.26552.115` but install under the untagged release version, for example `sdk/11.0.100`. Successive daily builds therefore share one on-disk folder, as does a stable `11.0.100` install.

After #56913, dotnetup detects this conflict and fails with a message telling the user to uninstall the owning install spec first. `dotnetup sdk update` for an RTM or servicing daily channel then needs a manual uninstall for every new build. This issue tracks doing the replacement automatically.

## Proposal

When a tracked install's on-disk folder belongs to a different build identity:

1. **Ask before replacing.** In interactive mode, show which install and which install specs will be replaced and ask for confirmation. In non-interactive mode, keep the current error unless an explicit opt-in is passed (for example `--replace` or `--yes`).
2. **Only replace what dotnetup owns.** Replace the folder only when every manifest record that uses it can be removed: records owned solely by the spec being updated, or specs the user confirmed. Never replace an untracked folder or one that a global.json spec still needs, unless the user explicitly confirms it.
3. **Replace atomically, and fail if files are in use.** Run under the install-state mutex:
   - Rename each affected folder to a sibling temp name, for example `sdk/.11.0.100.replacing-<guid>`. On failure, roll back any renames already done and report which folder is in use.
   - Extract the new payload into the original path.
   - On success, delete the renamed folders. If deletion fails, leave them for the garbage collector. On failure, restore them.
   - Update the manifest: remove the replaced records and add the new one.
4. **Cover bundled subcomponents.** An SDK archive also writes `shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App/<v>`, `shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<v>`, `host/fxr/<v>`, and packs. Today the extractor skips subcomponents that already exist, so a stale runtime from build A survives an update to build B. Before commit, list the archive's subcomponents. Treat each existing subcomponent owned by a different build identity as part of the same replacement set.

## In-use detection: needs investigation

Checking only the muxer isn't enough, because SDK and framework DLLs can also be in use.

- **Windows (NTFS):** renaming a directory fails when any file inside is open without `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`. Loaded DLLs and running executables are usually open that way. The rename test from step 3 should therefore be a reliable all-or-nothing check. Verify this with: a running `dotnet build` server (MSBuild node reuse), `dotnet watch`, a running app using the shared framework, the VS Code C# extension, and files opened by antivirus.
- **Linux, macOS and WSL (ext4 and similar):** renaming succeeds even while files are in use, because running processes keep the old inodes and continue on the old build. A rename can't detect use, though replacing is safe for running processes. Options:
  - Scan `/proc/*/maps` and `/proc/*/fd` for paths under the folder (Linux and WSL only; incomplete for other users' processes without privileges).
  - Accept replacement while files are in use and print a warning.
  - Use an advisory lock file that dotnetup-launched processes hold.
- **WSL on DrvFs (`/mnt/c/...`):** paths on the Windows drive behave differently from ext4, and a rename may fail like on Windows. Test both.
- **macOS:** behaves like Linux, but there's no `/proc`. Would need `lsof` or `proc_pidinfo`, or acceptance of replacement while in use.

Also decide whether `dotnetup` should hold a shared lock while running `dotnet` through `dotnetup dotnet`, so replacement can wait for or detect those processes.

## Tests

- Update build A to build B, both sharing a folder: the files and the manifest end up matching build B.
- Stable `11.0.100` already installed, then an RTM daily: prompt or error, and the stable install is untouched unless confirmed.
- A file inside the folder is held open (Windows): the replacement fails, the original folder is restored, and the manifest is unchanged.
- Non-interactive mode without the opt-in: the current error is unchanged.
- A bundled runtime subcomponent owned by a different build identity is replaced or reported.

## Related

- #56670: the original RTM daily install failure
- #56913: adds the conflict error this issue would replace
- #55311: dotnetup should not uninstall an SDK that is in use

Issues.Title: Hot Reload startup hook blocks app forever before Main when host handshake never completes (Visual Studio + Aspire)
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

When an Aspire AppHost is started with F5 in Visual Studio, one child project (an ASP.NET Core Blazor Server app) never reaches Main. The process is alive and the debugger is attached, but its main thread is blocked inside the Hot Reload startup hook (Listener.Listen -> InitializeAsync(...).GetAwaiter().GetResult()). There is no timeout, log output, warning or exception, so the app waits forever. Aspire shows the resource as "Running (Unhealthy)".

Turning off "Enable Hot Reload" in Visual Studio makes the project start normally, so the hang is caused by the Hot Reload handshake.

### Steps to reproduce

I don't have a minimal repro yet. What I do:

1. Open a solution with an Aspire AppHost (Aspire 13.6.4) containing a SQL database, a simple ASP.NET Core mock project, and the affected Blazor Server project as project resources.
2. In Tools > Options > Debugging > .NET/C++ Hot Reload, have "Enable Hot Reload" on.
3. Start the AppHost with F5 (debugger attached).
4. The affected project shows "Running (Unhealthy)" in the Aspire dashboard and never logs anything.
5. A breakpoint on the first line of Program.cs is never hit.
6. Use Debug > Break All, select the affected process, and look at its main thread: it is blocked in the Hot Reload startup hook.

The other project in the same AppHost starts fine with the same settings. The affected project also starts fine when run on its own from Visual Studio.

### Expected behavior

If the handshake with the Hot Reload host doesn't complete, the agent should time out and either log a warning and continue without Hot Reload, or fail with a clear error. A project shouldn't be able to hang indefinitely before Main with no diagnostics.

### Actual behavior

The app never starts. StartupHook.Initialize calls listener.Listen(CancellationToken.None), and Listen blocks on:

    // block execution of the app until initial updates are applied:
    InitializeAsync(cancellationToken).GetAwaiter().GetResult();

There is no timeout and it can't be cancelled. If the host never sends InitialUpdatesCompleted, the app waits forever.

Main thread stack (innermost first):

    [Managed to Native Transition]
    Monitor.Wait
    ManualResetEventSlim.Wait
    Task.SpinThenBlockingWait
    Task.InternalWaitCore
    Task.InternalWait
    TaskAwaiter.HandleNonSuccessAndDebuggerNotification
    [Waiting on Async Operation]
    Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Listener.Listen(CancellationToken)   Line 38
    StartupHook.Initialize()                                        Line 99
    MethodBaseInvoker.InvokeWithNoArgs
    StartupHookProvider.CallStartupHook
    StartupHookProvider.ProcessStartupHooks

The process loads the same modules as the working project up to System.Security.Claims.dll (Microsoft.Extensions.DotNetDeltaApplier.dll, System.IO.Pipes), then nothing more. Microsoft.AspNetCore.dll is never loaded, and a temporary File.WriteAllText as the first line of Program.cs never creates its file.

### Is this a regression?

Unknown. I haven't tested other Visual Studio, SDK or Aspire versions. I'm adding Aspire to an existing app, so I have no earlier working state under Aspire.

### Are there any workarounds?

Issues.Title: [release/10.0.4xx] Fix dotnet-watch project-update completion races
Issues.Body:
## Summary
Backport only the two `ProjectUpdateInProcTests` completion-wait fixes from https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/53424 (commit 96683a0ad81c5694820f7824342a4ca5079bdd64) to `release/10.0.4xx`.

Both reference-addition tests now wait up to 30 seconds for `ManagedCodeChangesApplied` before checking the remaining event counts. Application output can arrive before the watcher reports update completion, so checking the semaphore count immediately can fail with expected 1 / actual 0. Remove that count assertion because the wait consumes the semaphore.

Only one test file is changed; unrelated CI fixes from the original PR are excluded. No product behavior changes.

Relates to https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/53661
Relates to https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/56741

## Validation
- dotnet-watch.Tests built successfully with zero warnings or errors.
- Complete ProjectUpdateInProcTests class passed six runs (18/18 tests) on Windows using repo-local SDK 10.0.401 in installed-SDK/test-as-tool mode.

Issues.Title: Fix dotnetup RTM and servicing daily build installs
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56670.

RTM and servicing daily builds retain their build identity in the feed directory but publish archives with an untagged product-version filename. For example, the `11.0.1xx-daily` shortlink resolves to:

```text
https://ci.dot.net/public/Sdk/11.0.100-rtm.26552.115/dotnet-sdk-11.0.100-osx-arm64.tar.gz
```

Dotnetup tried to use `dotnet-sdk-11.0.100-rtm.26552.115-osx-arm64.tar.gz`, whose checksum does not exist.

# Complications

The RTM versions extract their layout onto the same versioned folder as the full GA release, so both `11.0.100-rtm.26552.115` and `11.0.100` use `11.0.100` for the on-disk layout. 

This means that only one can exist at a time per dotnet root. The `.version` file must be read to actually determine the version, and this is also true for the .NET Runtime installs.

Overlay / install exist checks become more complicated due to this, as the reasoning against folder names no longer always holds true. This is also true when a .NET SDK RTM version is tracked in the manifest, and we want to install a different RTM/GA Runtime, where the versions may not match but we have to demystify the install state to avoid incorrect behavior. 

# This change:

- Tries the product-version filename in the same build-specific directory only after the original checksum returns 404. 

- Carries the payload product version through verified downloads and installation artifacts. The tracked version remains the build identity, so daily updates can distinguish successive builds.

- Records optional `productVersion` metadata only when the on-disk version differs. Post-install validation, stale-entry pruning, verified listing, and update checks use it. Existing manifests without this property retain their current behavior.

- Documents why `dotnet --version` can report a release version for an RTM or servicing daily build.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Fix dotnetup RTM and servicing daily build installs" (#56913)

Issues.Title: Preserve invocation context during MTP strict-MT preparation
Issues.Body:
Strict-MT MTP preparation owns the process current directory until its MSBuild session ends. Parent-side operations must retain the invocation directory: otherwise background workload updates can miss repository `global.json` and `NuGet.Config`, and relative `DOTNET_CLI_TEST_TRACEFILE` paths can produce caught I/O exceptions and `MSB4287` while `dotnet test` exits successfully without the requested trace.

Capture the invocation directory before scheduling background updates and forward it through workload manifest discovery and the existing NuGet downloader override. Normalize and cache the trace path before managed MTP preparation starts. This preserves main's public `CommandServices` constructor contract, file-based execution, and strict-MT directory ownership without disabling updates or weakening MSBuild checks.

Follow-up to #56893. The matching release backport is #56908.

## Validation

- Managed CLI, shared-AOT compilation, and test builds passed with zero warnings or errors. Native publishing and native execution were not run.
- **75 focused cases passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, including workload configuration/local-feed lookup, trace logging, main's file-based no-build MT/legacy paths, `CommandServices` propagation, preparation failures, and multi-project/multi-TFM binlogs.
- The actual built SDK reproduced the baseline strict-MT relative-path failure: exit 0, 10 caught I/O exceptions, `MSB4287`, and no requested trace. After the fix, strict-MT relative, strict-MT absolute, legacy relative, and disabled-logging controls all exit 0 without those errors; enabled traces contain project-loading and test-process events.
- Current `dotnet.dll` and `Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.Utils.dll` were explicitly deployed into the redist layout, with matching SHA-256 hashes confirmed before and after the test runner.

Windows `win-x64`; built SDK `12.0.100-dev`, runtime `12.0.0-alpha.1.26528.111`, MSBuild `18.13.0-1.26528.111`, MTP `2.6.0-preview.26531.5`, and MSTest `4.6.0-preview.26531.5`. Bootstrap SDK: `12.0.100-alpha.1.26480.102`.

<details>
<summary>Exact commands and retained local diagnostics</summary>

```powershell
.\eng\build.ps1 -c Debug /p:PublishAot=false /p:_ShouldPublishDotnetAot=false /bl:artifacts\log\Debug\mtp-cwd-main-baseline.binlog
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe build src\Cli\dotnet\dotnet.csproj -c Debug --nologo -v:quiet -bl:artifacts\log\Debug\mtp-cwd-main-fixed-managed-build.binlog
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe build src\Cli\dotnet-aot\dotnet-aot.csproj -c Debug --nologo -v:quiet -bl:artifacts\log\Debug\mtp-cwd-main-fixed-shared-aot-build.binlog /p:PublishAot=false
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe build test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj -c Debug --nologo -v:quiet -bl:artifacts\log\Debug\mtp-cwd-main-fixed-tests-build.binlog --framework net12.0
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj --framework net12.0 --filter "FullyQualifiedName~GivenDotnetTestProducesBinaryLog|FullyQualifiedName~NuGetPackageDownloaderTests|FullyQualifiedName~GivenWorkloadManifestUpdater|FullyQualifiedName~GivenDotnetTestRunsFileBasedApps.RunWithNoBuildHonorsMultiThreading|FullyQualifiedName~GivenCommandServices" --test-binlogs
```

All commands exited 0. Runs used a process-local bounded `PATH`, `DOTNET_ADD_GLOBAL_TOOLS_TO_PATH=0`, `MSBUILDUSESERVER=0`, and `MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE=1`; user settings were not changed.

Issues.Title: Optimized NativeAOT publish skips runtime configuration hooks, breaking System.CommandLine executable-name injection
Issues.Body:
### Description

Updating from SDK `11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128` to `11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105` breaks System.CommandLine’s NativeAOT shared-library test on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

The optimized publish path introduced by dotnet/sdk#54515 skips `GenerateBuildRuntimeConfigurationFiles`. System.CommandLine contributes a runtime configuration item through this hook:

```xml
<Target Name="_AddSystemCommandLineExecutableName"
        DependsOnTargets="PrepareForBuild"
        BeforeTargets="GenerateBuildRuntimeConfigurationFiles">
  <ItemGroup>
    <RuntimeHostConfigurationOption
        Include="System.CommandLine.ExecutableName"
        Value="$(AssemblyName)"
        Trim="false" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Target>
```

Because the target no longer executes, the item never reaches NativeAOT’s compiler and is not embedded in the native image. The library publishes and loads successfully, but its executable name falls back to `dotnet` on Windows and `app` on macOS/Linux instead of `NativeLibrary`.

### Reproduction and evidence

The existing integration test in dotnet/command-line-api#2847 reproduces this by publishing a NativeAOT shared library and invoking an exported function that returns `new RootCommand().Name`.

- [Passing build with RC1](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1640186)
- [Failing build with RC2](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1643661)
- [Root-cause investigation](https://github.com/dotnet/command-line-api/pull/2847#issuecomment-6320900266)
- [System.CommandLine target at the failing revision](https://github.com/dotnet/command-line-api/blob/f894530bfd984e4ffeb53f1ec9e774b1409cb775/src/System.CommandLine/build/System.CommandLine.targets#L11-L25)

The tested revisions differ only in SDK/Arcade versions and dependency metadata.

### Expected behavior

Runtime configuration contributed by package targets remains available to NativeAOT publishing, or packages receive documented guidance identifying the supported hook replacing `GenerateBuildRuntimeConfigurationFiles`.

### Workaround

The SDK documents `UseOptimizedPublish=false` as the opt-out restoring the full build path.

Verified locally on macOS with SDK `12.0.100-alpha.1.26516.101`: after adding `<UseOptimizedPublish>false</UseOptimizedPublish>` to the NativeLibrary test project, the targeted Release integration test passed (1 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped):

```sh
dotnet test src/System.CommandLine.Tests/System.CommandLine.Tests.csproj -c Release -f net10.0 --filter FullyQualifiedName~RootCommand_name_falls_back_to_the_AppContext_value_when_hosted_as_a_native_library --no-restore
```

This validates the workaround on the local SDK; it has not yet been rerun on the original RC2 SDK or Windows/Linux.

### Related

 dotnet/sdk#56645 and dotnet/sdk#56649 address another consequence of the optimized publish path. That ordering fix does not restore `GenerateBuildRuntimeConfigurationFiles` or this hook.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.2xx] Honor MSBuild -mt in MTP test preparation
Issues.Body:
Backport of [#56893](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/56893) to `release/11.0.2xx`.

Retargeted from `release/11.0.1xx` without changing the backport commits.

Source commit: `2f0da079350a63d165b990e0cbfb3ead6bd09a58`.

MTP preparation honors explicit MSBuild `-mt` / `-multiThreaded` switches and environment precedence while preserving single-node execution, target-produced project state, and one coherent preparation binlog. Intervening builds/restores run out-of-process in the captured invocation directory only while a strict-MT preparation session owns the process current directory.

## Original-backport adaptations

These adaptations were made when preparing the original `release/11.0.1xx` backport:

- Retain the release branch's forwarding implementation and constructor contracts without importing main-only performance tracing or `CommandServices` changes.
- Include only the relevant MTP preparation contributor guidance.
- Omit the file-based-test regression and dispatch context: the corresponding `dotnet test` file-based implementation is not present on the original `release/11.0.1xx` target.

No dependency versions changed.

## Review corrections

Commit `6d21659a366cf21c390771f7e724ea0e997cd447` fixes two confirmed parent-process regressions that also affect the merged source change on main:

- **Background workload configuration:** preserve the existing public `RestoringCommand` constructor and add an internal explicit-directory overload. Pass the invocation directory through the background updater into both `global.json` discovery and the NuGet downloader's existing directory override. This prevents a due advertising update from selecting default/user feeds instead of repository-local configuration while the MT session is active. Foreground restore behavior, update gating, and signing policy are unchanged.
- **Relative diagnostic traces:** cache an absolute trace path and initialize the MTP logger before MSBuild can change process CWD. The previous behavior could lose the requested trace file and emit caught I/O exceptions plus MSB4287 even though the test command exited 0.

Added `BackgroundWorkloadUpdaterUsesTheCapturedInvocationDirectory` to verify the real workload provider, repository-only NuGet source mapping, and local package version lookup without network fallback. Added three real-product `ItKeepsTraceLoggingInTheInvocationDirectory` cases covering legacy relative paths, strict-MT relative paths, and an absolute-path MT control.

## Validation

The validation recorded below was performed for the original `release/11.0.1xx` backport. It is retained as historical evidence and has not been rerun as part of retargeting this PR to `release/11.0.2xx`.

- Managed CLI/test compilation and AOT managed/shared-source compilation succeeded. The latter reported zero warnings/errors. Native publishing was not exercised; only native publishing was disabled for the initial managed redist assembly, not product MT behavior or strict-mode checks.
- Final tests ran without rebuilding after explicitly deploying the committed CLI and utility outputs. SHA-256 hashes of the built/deployed DLLs matched before and after the entire run.
- Earlier initial-backport utility validation: **232 passed, 0 failed, 7 existing skips**. The review corrections do not change CLI utility source.

The release dependencies emit existing NuGet audit warnings (`MessagePack` 3.1.8 in the focused project, and `System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs` 8.0.1 in the full baseline build). Dependencies and audit settings were not changed or suppressed.

The process-local PATH setup avoids inherited temporary tool paths exceeding cmd.exe's lookup limit; it does not change user settings. Issues.Title: [release/11.0.2xx] Add inter-branch merge workflow into release/dnup
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Adds `.github/workflows/inter-branch-merge-flow-dnup.yml`, which opens automated merge PRs from `release/11.0.2xx` into `release/dnup`. This keeps dotnetup on .NET 11 instead of picking up `main`'s .NET 12 changes.

- **Trigger:** push to `release/11.0.2xx`.
- **Config:** calls Arcade's reusable `inter-branch-merge-base.yml` with `configuration_file_path: github-merge-flow-dnup.jsonc`. Like `github-merge-flow.jsonc`, the config is read from `main`.
- **Pinning:** the Arcade workflow and its scripts (`script_version`) are both pinned to the commit `main` already uses (`a1e2996a…`).
- **Telemetry:** sets `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_SESSIONID` at workflow scope, per the repo's CI telemetry guardrail.
- **Why a separate workflow:** this branch already flows to `main` through `inter-branch-merge-flow.yml`, and Arcade supports one merge target per branch per config file. The existing 11.0.2xx → main flow is unchanged.
- **Downstream:** the file will also flow forward to `main`, where it does nothing because its branch filter only matches `release/11.0.2xx`.

## Related PRs

- #56904: adds `github-merge-flow-dnup.jsonc` and removes the `main` → `release/dnup` flow
- #56903: one-time reset of `release/dnup` onto `release/11.0.2xx`

**Merge #56904 first.** Arcade's `read-configuration.ps1` fails, rather than skipping, when it can't fetch `github-merge-flow-dnup.jsonc` from `main`, so this workflow would fail on every `release/11.0.2xx` push until #56904 lands. If it does land first, rerun the failed workflow after #56904 merges; adding the file to `main` doesn't retrigger it.

## Validation

The YAML parses. The trigger, env, `uses`, and `with` inputs were checked, and `configuration_file_path` / `script_version` exist as inputs at the pinned Arcade commit.

Issues.Title: Flow release/11.0.2xx instead of main into release/dnup
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Stops `main` (now .NET 12) from flowing into `release/dnup`. dotnetup is fed from `release/11.0.2xx` instead, so it stays on .NET 11.

- **`github-merge-flow.jsonc`:**
  - Removes the `main` → `release/dnup` entry. It reset only `CODEOWNERS` on the assumption that dnup and main were the same 11.0 band, which is no longer true. That entry is how #56463 and #56707 brought .NET 12 into dotnetup.
  - Removes the stale `dnup` source entry. That branch no longer exists.
- **New `github-merge-flow-dnup.jsonc`:** maps `release/11.0.2xx` → `release/dnup` and resets only `CODEOWNERS`. Dependency and toolset files are not reset because `release/dnup` has no darc subscription; this merge is its only update path.
  - It's a separate file because Arcade's [read-configuration.ps1](https://github.com/dotnet/arcade/blob/main/.github/workflows/scripts/read-configuration.ps1) supports one `MergeToBranch` per source branch per config file, and `release/11.0.2xx` already flows to `main`.
  - Like the existing config, it's read from `main`.
- **`documentation/project-docs/SDK-PR-guide.md`:** documents the dnup flow.

## Related PRs

- #56903: one-time reset of `release/dnup` onto `release/11.0.2xx`, plus a net11 TFM guard
- #56905: adds `inter-branch-merge-flow-dnup.yml`, which runs the merge using this config

**Merge this PR before #56905.** Arcade's `read-configuration.ps1` fails, rather than skipping, when it can't fetch the configuration file, so #56905's workflow would fail on every push to `release/11.0.2xx` until this file exists on `main`. When a newer .NET 11 band is created, move the source key here and the workflow trigger to that branch.

After this merges, close the pending `merge/main-to-release/dnup` PR.

## Validation

Both config files parse with `ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashTable`, the same parser Arcade uses. The resolved mappings are correct.
